narrative.overview:
StoryQuestor is a creator's workshop. The aesthetic is kinetic and purposeful: hot amber energy on deep ink-night backgrounds in the editor, cool white parchment in the reader. Two distinct thermal zones, both serving the same forge metaphor. Where the editor feels like a craftsperson hammering a narrative into shape, the reader feels like holding the finished object in your hands.

The system rejects productivity-tool aesthetics. No Notion-clone white cards with blue primary buttons. No gray dashboards that could belong to any SaaS product. Color here earns its place: amber marks the primary creative action, violet traces the structural shimmer, teal marks chapter transitions. Each accent has a semantic role, not a decorative one.

Energy without overwhelm is the governing tension. The palette is rich but never garish; motion feedback is immediate but never theatrical. A first-time creator should feel invited, not auditioned.
keyCharacteristics: Dual thermal zones: dark forge (editor, nav) and bright page (reader, cards)
Full palette with four named accent roles, each semantically distinct
Geist Sans across all weights; hierarchy through scale and weight contrast
Shadows respond to state, not decoration: flat at rest, lifted on interaction
Rounded edges throughout (8-16px) signal approachability without softness
Gradient amber-to-orange reserved for the single most important CTA on any surface

rules.name: The One Gradient Rule
rules.body: The amber-to-orange gradient belongs to primary CTAs and the logo mark only. It is the hottest point of the forge; dilute it and you lose the hierarchy.

rules.name: The Ink Night Rule
rules.body: Dark backgrounds always carry the purple-shifted ink tones (#1a1025, #0f172a), never neutral dark grays. Pure gray backgrounds on dark surfaces are forbidden.

rules.name: The Weight Ladder Rule
rules.body: Each step in the hierarchy requires at minimum a 1.25x size ratio or a two-step weight jump. Similar size with different weights is not enough separation.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: No element starts with a shadow as decoration. The resting state is flat. Shadows appear in response to hover, focus, or modal elevation only.

dos: Use the amber-to-orange gradient exclusively on the single highest-priority CTA per surface.
Use Ink Night (#1a1025) and Deep Slate (#0f172a) for all dark surfaces.
Express hierarchy through type weight and size contrast: at least 1.25x size ratio or two weight steps between adjacent levels.
Let shadows respond to state: shadow-sm at rest, shadow-md or higher on hover or elevation.
Use rounded corners throughout: 8px for buttons/inputs, 12px for cards and nodes, 16px for modals.
Tint every neutral toward the brand hue. Ink Night is purple-tinted, not charcoal.
Keep body text within 65-75ch in reading contexts.
donts: Don't use generic SaaS aesthetics: no Notion-clone white cards with blue primary buttons.
Don't use pure black (#000000) or pure white (#ffffff) as backgrounds.
Don't apply the amber-to-orange gradient to more than one element per surface.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on cards or list items.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text). Use solid colors and weight/size for emphasis.
Don't add decorative shadows. Every shadow communicates state or structure.
Don't mix more than two accent colors on a single screen without semantic justification.
Don't use glassmorphism as a default aesthetic.
Don't use neutral dark grays for dark backgrounds; use the purple-shifted Ink Night palette.
